what: The screen is pinned at 2600px and a frame set (171 frames by default) advances with scroll so the product rotates and comes apart — the frame number is progress/0.8 split by the frame count and rounded (the last frame lands at 80% of the pin). The stage settles with expo.out from 75% below, 1.15×, .5 opacity and 8px blur, starting when 5% of the section reaches 80% of the screen until the section’s top edge touches the top of the screen, and when 85% of the section reaches the bottom of the screen the first child slips 20% upward with power2.in. Once progress passes .65, the part labels turn on together with the underline (.25s later .75s) and end dot (.5s)

options.frames: Frame Count — If there is one, that count, otherwise this value (default 171). The side that uses the fx:frame event draws it
options.end: Progress reaching the end frame, default .8
options.drift: First-child upward shift on exit (%), default -20

use: — images use img[data-fx-part=frame] group, or el.addEventListener('fx:frame', e => draw(e.detail.progress))
note: The original preloads 171 sequence images. If frames are image files, they must all be downloaded before the first draw or steps appear — the part draws only the frames received and skips numbers not yet loaded

from.where: index.html [data-slot=sticky-sprite] — a section where a watch turns from front view to side view and becomes an exploded diagram
